answer: A single sonnet checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a sable, before it can post or attest. Forging 431 aliases as a result costs 344 bonds held for 4 days each, plus the vertex attestations those aliases can never earn. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
